title: Pratt's group construction for T_k: affine maps over ℤ₂ need a group of order at least 2^{3k−1}
statement: Let T_k = Σ x_S y_T z_U over the ordered partitions (S, T, U) of [3k] into k-sets. A quadruple (f₁, f₂, f₃, x), f_i from k-subsets to a finite abelian group G and x ∈ G, is valid if f₁(S) + f₂(T) + f₃(U) = x holds exactly for the ordered partitions; for G = 𝔽₂^m a valid quadruple gives R(T_k) ≤ 2^m over every field of characteristic ≠ 2 (Theorem 1; the principle of Pratt's arXiv:2311.02774v1, §1.2, item 4, extended to three maps). (1) For every k, the vectors 1 + 1_S + 1_T + 1_U over all triples of k-subsets of [3k] are exactly the even-weight vectors of 𝔽₂^{3k}. (2) For G = 𝔽₂^m and affine maps f_i(S) = L_i(1_S) + b_i, the quadruple is valid if and only if L₁, L₂, L₃ agree on the even-weight code E, L₁ is injective on E, and x = f₁(S₀) + f₂(T₀) + f₃(U₀) for one fixed ordered partition (S₀, T₀, U₀); hence m ≥ 3k − 1, and for m = 3k − 1 the quadruple is valid if and only if the maps agree on E, x is as stated, and the kernel of L₁ is spanned by a single vector of odd weight (the coordinate-deletion map is such a construction). So no affine instantiation of the method, with one map or three different maps, uses a group of order below 2^{3k−1}. (3) For arbitrary maps into any finite abelian group, |G| ≥ 2·C(3k, k) − C(2k, k); for G = ℤ₂^m this gives m ≥ 3k − 1 exactly when k ≤ 3, and the bound is below 2^{3k−2} for every k ≥ 4.

bases: Pratt 2023, arXiv:2311.02774v1, §1.2, item 4 of the comments after Corollary 1.12 (the group construction for R(T_k) ≤ 2^{3k−1})
